title: QCon San Francisco 2026: The Harness Is the New Operating System
summary:
At QCon San Francisco 2026, Mad Labs founder and CEO Manju Rajashekhar opened the conference arguing that the harness around an AI model, rather than the model itself, decides what an agent can do and how safely it does it. The keynote mapped the parts of a harness, including context, tools, state, permissions and feedback loops, onto jobs that operating systems already perform.

By Andrew Hoblitzell

title: PostgreSQL 19 Released with Online Table Repacking and Query Planning Controls
summary:
The PostgreSQL Global Development Group released PostgreSQL 19, introducing changes to database maintenance, query planning, replication, and application development. The release focuses on reducing administrative overhead and improving performance, with new tools for reorganizing tables without downtime and controlling query plans.

By Robert Krzaczyński

title: Claude Code Has Been Leaking Secrets through its "Don't Ask Again" Feature
summary:
Agentic security firm Apiiro found that Claude Code has been exposing secrets in public repositories due to how it stores them in local file on developers' machines to implement "Don't Ask Again". The company identified 1,122 secrets in claude/settings.local.json files and another 1,160 in git history, in the shared settings.json, and in agent chat transcripts stored in repos.

By Sergio De Simone

title: Google Announces Agent Compute Engine for Secure AI Agent Execution
summary:
Google recently announced Agent Compute Engine, a managed service that runs AI agents in isolated microVMs, with checkpointing capabilities to suspend and resume execution environments. The design keeps credentials, API keys, and OAuth refresh tokens outside the agent sandbox, using an external Agent Gateway to authenticate requests and inject the required secrets.

By Renato Losio

title: AWS Lambda Now Runs GPU Inference with 48 Concurrent Invocations Sharing One Model per GPU
summary:
AWS Lambda now runs Event Functions on EC2 G-series GPU instances through Lambda Managed Instances, with up to 48 concurrent invocations sharing one model per GPU, vLLM and SGLang base images that need no handler code, and 90-minute asynchronous timeouts. Billing is the instance price plus a 9.75 percent fee; first hands-on tests report an eight-minute publish and no response streaming.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers

title: Uber Cuts Translation Cache Memory by up to 90% While Keeping P99 Latency below 1 MS
summary:
Uber redesigned its Go-based translation cache to reduce its initial memory footprint by more than 90% while maintaining a cache hit rate above 99.9% and p99 disk-backed cache miss latency below 100 microseconds. The hybrid architecture combines in-memory keys and frequently accessed values with disk-backed storage, reducing garbage-collection overhead and memory consumption.

By Leela Kumili

title: Presentation: Modernising Retail at Scale: Architecting a Cloud‑to‑Edge Platform for a Global Enterprise
summary:
Jayesh Bhayani discusses Tesco’s decade-long enterprise transformation from fragmented legacy systems to a unified cloud-edge platform. He explains how aligning system, talent, and process modernizations allowed Tesco to scale mission-critical retail operations to millions of customers, while sharing practical lessons on build vs. buy, cloud cost management, and preparing for agentic commerce.

By Jayesh Bhayani

title: QCon San Francisco 2026: the Future of Apache Iceberg
summary:
Apache Iceberg V4 proposes a redesign of table metadata to improve scalability and support more frequent writes, alongside new capabilities for data management and schema evolution. Daniel Weeks, co-creator of Apache Iceberg and member of technical staff at Databricks, presented a session at QCon San Francisco on the fourth version of the Apache Iceberg open table format specification.

By Renato Losio

title: Article: Building Reliability into the Cloud: Observability as the Control Plane for Multi-Region Failover
summary:
Cloud SLAs promise uptime statistically, not absolutely. This article shows how to treat observability as a control plane that detects regional degradation, triggers automated failover, and confirms recovery rather than paging a human. Covers active-active architecture, DNS TTL pitfalls, composite Prometheus alerting, Route 53 weighted routing, and confirmation loops backed by a real S3 outage.

By Saurabh Ahuja

title: AWS Releases a Free Local Emulator of AWS Built Entirely by Agents
summary:
AWS has released AWS Emulator, a free, CC0-licensed local stand-in for more than 200 of its services, generated from its public API models and aimed at the test loops of coding agents. AWS says agents wrote and maintain all of the code and publishes per-release fidelity scores. The docs say it does not evaluate IAM, and practitioners are split on trusting an emulator nobody reviewed.

By Steef-Jan Wiggers
